title: Scikit-Learn Logistic Regression Pipeline on the Breast Cancer Dataset
description: Split load_breast_cancer() using the supplied ratio with stratify=y, fit a StandardScaler + LogisticRegression pipeline, and evaluate with classification_report, ConfusionMatrixDisplay, and RocCurveDisplay.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Load `data = load_breast_cancer()`, extract `X = data.data` and `y = data.target`, and split into train and test sets using the supplied ratio with `stratify=y`.

Build `pipe` with `StandardScaler(with_mean=True)` and `LogisticRegression` using the supplied iteration limit and C. Fit it on `(X_train, y_train)`, compute `y_pred` and `y_prob = pipe.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]`, and print `classification_report`.

Compare how `y_pred` and `y_prob` are used downstream: `confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred, ...)` on line 20 counts thresholded 0/1 decisions, while `roc_curve(y_test, y_prob)` on line 27 sweeps across the continuous class-1 probabilities.

steps.question: In the classification report on lines 16-17, how many test samples belong to each class (`support`), and what overall test accuracy does `pipe` reach?
steps.answer: There are `53` `malignant` samples and `90` `benign` samples (`143` total in `y_test`), and `pipe` achieves `0.99` accuracy (`0.98` F1 on `malignant`, `0.99` F1 on `benign`).

steps.description: Plot the `2 x 2` confusion matrix with `ConfusionMatrixDisplay` and plot the ROC curve with `RocCurveDisplay` and `roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr)`.
